validity.researcher_notes: STARTED FROM THE SHEET'S OWN CITATION per the brief: fetched https://egyptoil-gas.com/reports_category/monthly/page/7/ directly (both via url_verifier and a manual HTML fetch). It 200s but is confirmed to be nothing more than a paginated 'Monthly Reports' category archive listing ten unrelated report titles (Nov 2020-Aug 2021) plus nav chrome -- it never contains 'El-Hafair', 'Suez', or any of this row's numbers. url_verifier FAILs on every value token (Hafair, 35, 18, 50,000) from this URL. Per the task brief this kind of generic/aggregate non-naming citation is itself an existence flag, so I chased it: gem.wiki's own citation text names the source as the 'Monthly Reports - Part 7/ September 2020 edition' -- so I went looking for the actual September 2020 EOG article instead of the broken index link. Found it: 'Gulf of Suez, Eastern Desert and Sinai: Egypt's Crude Oil Squad' (egyptoil-gas.com/reports/gulf-of-suez-eastern-desert-and-sinai-egypts-crude-oil-squad/, datePublished 2020-09-07T09:54:20+02:00, i.e. Egypt Oil & Gas Newspaper, September 2020, Issue 165). This URL serves as a raw PDF body under a text/html header (confirmed by byte-inspection: response starts '%PDF-1.6', Adobe InDesign 15.0, 4 pages) -- exactly the 'large/compressed PDF' false-negative pattern url_verifier.py's own docstring warns about (large PDFs aren't fully text-extracted by the substring screen), which is why the raw verifier check FAILs on 'Hafair' even though the content is there; verifier passes on 'Suez' alone (liveness confirmed) and I manually downloaded the PDF and ran `pdftotext -layout` myself to confirm the rest. Page 12-13 carries a table headed 'Crude Oil Infrastructure in the Gulf of Suez/Sinai' listing 'the Gulf of Suez and Sinai's mainly eight crude oil pipelines' with columns From/To/Length(Km)/Diameter(Inches)/Capacity(bbl/d), crediting EGPC's data. The row 'Al Hafair-Suez: Al Hafair -> Suez, 35, 18, 50,000' is an EXACT match on every GEM value for P7976. The same table also carries 'Ras Shukheir-Al Hafair: 215/26/140,000' (= P7975 exactly), and two 'Al Hafair-Mostorod' rows at 135/18-20/85,000 and 115/24/85,000 (= P7977 and P7978 exactly) -- so this one table is the real common primary source behind the whole El-Hafair family bulk-loaded 2026-03-15/16, and it is NOT GEM-derived (an Egyptian oil-industry trade newspaper, sourced to EGPC). Classification confirmed: the source's own text calls it one of the region's crude-oil TRANSMISSION pipelines (as distinct from field gathering lines discussed elsewhere in the same issue), matching GEM's PipelineType=transmission / Fuel=Oil. Cross-checked the routes-repo geometry (P7976.geojson, 3-vertex line from ~29.737N/32.376E near the OSM-confirmed locality 'الحفائر' (El-Hafair), Suez governorate, through to ~29.960N/32.533E at Suez) -- geographically consistent with a ~35 km corridor, corroborating plausibility (not counted as an independent source, per rule 1). Checked this scope's OSM and GulfPub recon runs (batches/egypt-oil/staging/recon-{osm,gulfpub}-20260827/match_diff.json) for independent corroboration: NEITHER supports it. GulfPub's two 'additions' scored against P7976 (Safir-Meleiha, Kalabsha-Khepri) are unrelated Western Desert oilfield gathering lines that only coincidentally share a similar length (~30.5-30.6 km vs GEM's 35 km) -- false-positive length matches, not real overlaps (both NEAR_MISS/DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE, composite scores 0.28-0.35, well below threshold; no name or route match). OSM's two 'additions' against P7976 are both red-confidence and below threshold too (0.17 and 0.29 composite) -- one unnamed way partially inside P7976's own drawn route (FRAGMENT_OF_EXISTING, not new information), the other a short unnamed stub scored on length alone. So this remains a SINGLE strong, on-point, exact-match primary source, not two independent ones -- I could not find a second (WebSearch quota was exhausted this session at 200/200; targeted WebFetch probes at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum_Pipelines_Company and egyptoil-gas.com's own site search for 'Al Hafair' both came back empty). Tier stays medium, not high, on that basis, despite the strength/specificity of the one match. Duplicate check against the full 46-row Egypt-oil roster: NOT a duplicate of P7975 (Ras Shukheir->El-Hafair, different route/diameter/capacity), P7977 or P7978 (El-Hafair->Mostorod, different destination and diameter/capacity) -- the primary source itself lists all four as distinct pipelines in one table, each with its own length/diameter/capacity, radiating from the same Al Hafair junction station; this is a real small hub network, not a bulk duplicate or relabel.

validity.researcher_notes: The Sept 2020 EOG article explicitly names PPC as operator only for SUMED ('operated by the Petroleum Pipeline Company (PPC)'); it does not repeat an operator attribution for the Al Hafair-family lines described immediately afterward in the same table/section. PPC is Egypt's dedicated national crude/product pipeline operating company under EGPC and is the standard operator for EGPC-owned domestic crude trunklines across this scope, so the sheet's Operator=PPC / Owner1=EGPC 100% is a reasonable default and I found nothing contradicting it in any source read -- but it is inference from industry structure, not an explicit per-line statement, so this stays a caveat rather than a fresh confirmation. No ref change proposed for Operator/Owner beyond what applies to the rest of the row (same broken page-7 citation, same fix).
